notes.title: Development Update 4, July.
notes.notes:
[h1]So, what's been going on?[/h1]

Throughout July I've been working on a lot of different things. This has definitely been the most improvements I have made to the game so far, I'll try and list as many as I can with the largest improvements getting small dedicated sections. 

[h2]Level Design[/h2]

The cameras within the game have been changed from being "camera 1" to the named areas below. 
[list]
[*] Abandoned Construction
[*] Muddy River 
[*] Crumbling Stone 
[*] Deep Forest
[/list]

this will allow players to identify where the dinosaur is easier, as some of the areas will have sound cues to let the player know. E.g. Crumbling stone plays a "rocks falling" sound whenever the dinosaur is near it. 
This also allows me to be more creative with each area and what it should look like. You can see the new versions of each area in the images below. (All of these images are taken during the day so that they are easily visible, but you will mainly see them during the night). 

[h3]Abandoned Construction[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/9fc7872fbe25ce9186fbf62bea6fc79de1b12686.png[/img]

[h3]Muddy River[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/2b3aaf307f8701d29cc2e3bce640455c904dc18e.png[/img]

[h3]Crumbling Stone[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/9f5a7e92619808b5c84d4427669525974d7affe8.png[/img]

[h3]Deep Forest[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/9c0b5c7713e1f0350fa354b6ae4c8af43275f2ad.png[/img]

[h2]Optimization[/h2]
Something that I've been struggling with in creating the game is keeping it optimised so that it runs at a reasonable FPS. Well, I spent some time on it during July. The game would be inconsistent, sometimes running at an FPS that seemed super low for everything that the game is. Here's what I've changed to fix this: 

[list]
[*] Removed the grass from the ground (this LITERALLY added 30fps as the grass was loading all at once and had its own small animations, I'll look into replacing it with something less destructive). 
[*] Removed any unused assets, including cutting the map size down to be smaller (the playable area was not made smaller) 
[*] Removed shadows from certain assets such as trees, I might add a way to turn these back on for people with high tier systems. 
[*] The biggest thing was that I turned off Lumen and some other beta lighting from UE5. This added the largest FPS boost and honestly the game seems super smooth now. 
[/list]

Each level will be locked to 60fps to stop the game suffering from any fps spikes and drops. 

[h2]Objective Markers[/h2]
I found while playing the game that the player would probably get quite lost without being directly shown where to go for specific things. E.g. go find the red generator. Well each building has a red generator to power building. So I've made a tutorial of sorts on the first day level. This allows the player to experience a few mechanics before jumping into the rest of the game. The plan is to have it so that objectives are not always on the screen and that they only appear if its something urgent the player needs to do or something new that they haven't done before. Alternatively I can paint everything with yellow paint to scream "go here" lol. A short video showing off objectives and some new voice lines can be found below. 

[previewyoutube=pRUuOJs4zgA;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Red generator opens doors[/h2]
From the video above you can see that at one point I pick up a gas cannister and use it on a red generator. This then opens the doors to the building (Operations building). This mechanic is to make sure the player cant just get into every building. Each level will have a certain amount of cannisters that you can find and you can use them on any of the buildings in any order. It also saves between levels, you open the operations building on level 1, when you go to level 2 it is already open. 

[h2]Random chance of rain[/h2]
Every time you boot up one of the levels there is a set chance that in game it will start raining. This is to add both atmosphere and more variety to the weather. An image of the rain at night can be found below. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/8caefe4b7d3d8e60b2a95f37df94f0c741fdd3b0.png[/img]

[h2]Cameras can now lose power[/h2]
Within the game, depending on how much the player uses their flashlight (the one of the cameras) or the shocking system on the fences (used to deter the dinosaur). The cameras can now go down by the power "tripping". How it works: Player starts off with 0% chance >>> player used electric shock +10% >>> player uses flashlight twice +2.5 each time >>> game checks percentage, if it hits then the power cuts off and the player must restore it using the generator shown in earlier dev updates. Below is an image of what it looks like (for the demo) when the power goes out on the cameras. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/e4a9eb9d5c960b29bdf66dfd2be17f2c95e91eba.png[/img]

[h2]Camera flashlight rework and Electric shock update[/h2]
So how the flashlight used to work was the player could turn it on and off whenever they wanted and it didn't add any chance to the power tripping. Now the flashlight can only be turned on. How it works: Player pressed flashlight button >>> flashlight is turned on and after 5 seconds (this may change) the flashlight turns off >>> +2.5 is added to chance of power tripping and player can now turn the flashlight back on again. The flashlight also turns on for EVERY camera. So if you need to switch between cameras after using the flashlight, you can do it without having to press the flashlight again. 

The electric shock has not changed much, player presses it, the screen goes black, shock recharges, player can use it again. Each time it is used it adds +10 to the chance of the power tripping. It feels like its in a good spot. 

To help with the player knowing what the chance of the power tripping is, I've added a UI widget in the bottom left of the CCTV cameras, a small battery that starts all white at 0% and gradually goes from green to red depending on power usage. Below is an image of the UI when the chance is 100% to show off the different stages. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45011813/5ff249605f59447d8248bf288e71eed89d719144.png[/img]

[h2]Other parts of the game that are being worked on[/h2]

[list]
[*] Pause menu (in the game currently but its very basic)
[*] Turning sound up and down (also in the game but not complete) 
[*] Credits section for the game 
[*] Voice lines for night levels and some more for the first level
[*] A less impactful way of making the ground look more realistic (basically better grass)
[*] A lot of bug fixing for minor things such as widgets not disappearing correctly. 
[/list]

[h2]So what's next? Will there be a demo? [/h2]
Over the next month I plan on getting a lot of the "glue" work done. Anything that is missing that needs to be in the game to improve gameplay flow. Expect an update about that near the end of August. 

And yes there will be a demo, not much more I can say about that for now. 

Thanks for reading this development update, your continued support motivates me to make the best game that I can currently make. 

P.s. Special thanks to Bestinslot on YouTube for covering my game in one of his latest videos.

notes.title: Development Update 3 - Voice lines, Subtitles, Objective markers...
notes.notes:
[h1]Development Update 3[/h1]

[h2]A quick update on being a solo dev[/h2]
With this game being a solo project, development times are reliant on me. This means that I have to balance creating this game around my university work and my full time work at Game/Gamestop. 
So I'm happy to say that I've finished my semester of university! This should mean that development picks up a bit and that I'll be able to share more updates. Either way, thank you for the continued support. 

[h2]How I'll be posting updates from now on[/h2]
Instead of posting "week 3/4/5 development update" I'll now instead post updates like this "development update 3 - added new stuff" this allows me to not have to post every single week and to focus on development, only posting when I have something cool to show off. 

[h2]Voice lines & Subtitles[/h2]
Recently I was able to record and then edit some voice lines to test for the game! These are not final and the dialogue may change. How it works is I record myself speaking in audacity and then change the EQ, cut down the audio and do a bunch of checks to make sure there is no random background noise. (Recording these from my bedroom) 

[previewyoutube=1VSsnslw1_U;full][/previewyoutube]

After adding voice lines I decided it would be a good idea to add subtitles as it would make it easier for everyone to understand what I'm saying, especially people not accustomed to an Irish accent. 
These are easy enough to implement but depending on how many voice lines the game may have, it could end up being very time consuming. 

[h2]Objective Markers[/h2]
While getting the game ready for a playable demo, I realised that players are going to have a hard time figuring out exactly where to go when playing the game, so I've added objective markers. The player should only ever have one at a time and it will guide them to a location. e.g. at the start of the game, the player will have an objective marker that brings them to the operations building. 

[previewyoutube=0PBwOMD14us;full][/previewyoutube]

As always there have been improvements in the scripting of the game as well as the overall feel of some of the mechanics, a noteworthy improvement is the ability to now "enhance" text whenever a player picks up a note, this will allow players who have a hard time reading the text, the ability to read it in a cleaner format. 

That's it from me for now, thanks for reading!

notes.title: WEEK 1 Development Update - New doors, new skys and a thank you.
notes.notes:
[h1]Thank you![/h1]

The first week of being on Steam has been an overwhelming success. My goal for the first week was to hit 50 wishlists. We ended up hitting over 60+! So, from the bottom of my heart thank you so much. Wishlisting the game helps support development as it allows me to gauge interest while also giving me a little boost in happiness. 

[h2]New additions to the game.[/h2]

Instead of rambling on about every little tiny bit of blueprinting I did, I thought I would list them. 
[list]
[*] New doors were added to the game and placed in all buildings, replacing the older, buggy models. 
[*] New "garage" doors were added to specific buildings that required them. 
[*] New day time sky was added, while I've not fully decided on how it will look, it already looks 10x better. 
[*] New night time sky added, instead of being pitch black the game now has stars and a moon, allowing for better vision but you'll still need to use your torch! 
[*]New volumetric height fog was added, this does so much for the atmosphere!
[/list]

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Fixed a problem with the players height, which stopped them from getting through doors sometimes. 
[*] Fixed a problem with the pathways sitting higher than the ground, creating an area in which you could see under the pathways. 
[*] Fixed lighting problems, but will need looked at again to make it more to my liking. 
[*] Fixed collisions on doors. 
[*] Fixed collision boxes not working when trying to interact with garage doors and doors. 
[*] Fixed and adjusted a lot of the buildings, the models I'm using seem to have a lot of problems with not being the correct size, meaning I have to manually adjust them all the time. 
[/list]

Thank you for taking the time to read this, feel free to get in contact if you have any questions or feedback. Remember to join the discord here: https://discord.gg/byZBSYcKMY
